newsitem.title: USA: Senate approves new ship subsidy plan.
newsitem.headline: Senate approves new ship subsidy plan.

text.p: The Senate Tuesday approved a bill setting up a new U.S.-flag shipping subsidy plan under which the vessels would be available for carrying defence supplies during wartime.

Under the bill operators of U.S.-flag ships that could be used for military supply purposes would receive $2.3 million for each ship this year and $2.1 million for each ship annually through fiscal 2005. The bill authorised $100 million a year for the payments.

The bill, approved on an 88-10 vote, would replace the current programme that provides government payments to U.S.-flag operators based on the difference between the crew and operating costs of U.S.-flag vessels and foreign-flag ships.
Operating American ships costs more because of higher pay and benefits and more costly regulation.
The plan was assailed by a Senate foe, Sen Charles Grassley, R-Iowa, as "welfare" for shipping companies and unions but supporters said its cost would be half of that of the current programme.

But Sen. Daniel Inouye, D-Hawaii, said the new plan would guarantee the Defence Department a pool of American crews and a 50-ship fleet of militarily useful ships, along with the companies' railcars, containers and other facilities.
"We must be able to ensure that U.S.-flag shipping is available to bring materiel and ammunition to soldiers who are defending our interests on foreign soil," said Inouye.

Sen. Ted Stevens, R-Alaska, said that more than 120 U.S.-flag ships were called on to help the U.S. military buildup in the Gulf prior to the Gulf war. At the same time some foreign operators doubled their normal charter rates.
Under the new plan, U.S. shipping firms would have to agree to rates established in advance for chartering in a defence emergency.
The bill, which had administration support, must now be reconciled with a similar House-passed measure.
